Proper scoring rules define a class of functions S(P, y) that penalize forecast distributions P given realized outcomes y such that truthful reporting minimizes expected score. This duality enables dual roles: evaluating forecasts via S(P, Q) = E_Y~Q[S(P, Y)] and estimating distributions by minimizing S(P, y) over data. The characterization theorem shows that every regular proper score equals a Bregman divergence of an entropy function, which provides a unified geometric interpretation. Kernel scores (like CRPS) arise from integral representations involving energy statistics, while local scores (like Brier) correspond to pointwise evaluations. These distinctions inform GSI’s use of Bayesian inference for generating predictive distributions and GSE’s dynamic evolution of those distributions through state transitions guided by score-based feedback loops.
